- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods of the 30-day forecast, especially when recent history shows upward momentum.
- Overestimates prices after sharp spikes in the history (e.g., 60+ → 70+), often overshooting by 5–15% and failing to account for subsequent mean reversion.
- Underestimates prices during periods of sustained downward trend (e.g., 60–55 range) — model appears to “hold too low” rather than adjusting for momentum.
- Shows lag in responding to recent high values — true prices often rise faster than model predicts, especially in the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- Tends to overcorrect after minor dips — model may “bounce back too early” or underestimate the depth of a correction.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model often fails to recognize that prices will return to prior averages after sharp moves, especially in the 10–15 day window.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 10 days — model is most inaccurate in the initial segment, with accuracy improving toward the end of the 30-day horizon.
- When history includes multiple consecutive high values, model tends to overpredict the next value, ignoring the diminishing marginal effect of recent peaks.
